column2: The emigrant assemblies around the Vet River are gathering under a common raad. Winburg will provide a single seat for the southern trekker government, maintaining its existing diplomatic obligations.

The captaincies draw together Griqua families, Khoisan communities and Dutch-speaking frontier households. Their institutions rest on these local connections.
Griekwastad and the country around Vooruitzigt belong to distinct districts within the western Griqua claim. Their names and jurisdictions should not be confused.

The Free State offers to purchase the captaincy's sovereign rights at Philippolis. Adam Kok's council must decide whether to accept compensation or retain its frontier jurisdiction.
The captaincy at Philippolis retains rights that were not extinguished by the Orange River Convention. A compensated agreement with its council can settle the disputed jurisdiction.

Surveyors, interpreters and magistrates can record competing claims before disputes become armed confrontations. Existing occupation and customary grazing rights deserve a hearing alongside settler titles.
The Cost of the Orange River Sovereignty
Maintaining magistrates and a garrison beyond the Orange places growing demands on the Cape treasury. A temporary appropriation can support the administration while ministers reconsider its future.

The diggings have drawn miners into a landscape of overlapping Griqua, settler and imperial claims. Hearings and registered concessions may restrain speculative seizures, though they cannot erase the competing claims.

Dutch control of the Cape offers merchants a renewed place on the southern sea route. Local contracts, bilingual clerks and recognition of established property claims can encourage trade without reviving the old Company monopoly.
A restored Dutch administration needs teachers familiar with the Cape's languages and local communities. An endowed training institution can support a lasting school system.

The settlement around the diggings at Vooruitzigt has grown into a substantial town. Kimberley is becoming its established name, while Griekwastad remains a separate western district.
